//: Cases every Treebars SDK runs against its own implementation, shared so that the SDKs cannot disagree. Generated; do not edit.

scenarios.name: an acknowledged batch is removed, and one flush drains the queue batch by batch
any 2xx is an acknowledgement, not only 200
a network failure keeps the sealed batch, out of the queue, behind a jittered gate
every retry resends the same batch, nothing is sent before the gate, and an acknowledgement resumes the drain
a relaunch resends the pending batch with its batch_id before anything tracked since
events tracked while a batch is pending go in the next batch, and the pending one never grows
one flush sends at most drain_max_batches batches, and the next flush carries on
the drain stops at the first failure and seals nothing further
backoff is full jitter under a doubling ceiling that stops at the cap, and success resets it
429 honours Retry-After in seconds: no random delay is drawn, and nothing is sent before it
503 honours Retry-After as an HTTP date, measured from now
Retry-After is capped at retry_after_max_seconds, in both of its forms
a Retry-After that is absent, unreadable, zero, negative, fractional, past, or on another status falls back to jitter
a relaunch does not hammer: the Retry-After gate is persisted and still holds
401 keeps the batch and starts a persisted cooldown that a relaunch does not reset
403 starts the same cooldown, and a build with a different write key is not held to it
the first send after a cooldown is a probe, and a second refusal starts another cooldown
413 splits the batch in half, each half gets a derived batch_id, and the halves are sent in turn
a split is persisted: a failure on the first half keeps both halves pending across a relaunch
a half that is still too large splits again, and a single event still too large is dropped, which ends the flush
any other 4xx drops the batch, resets the backoff, and ends the flush
a clock set backwards cannot hold uploads past the retry gate's own ceiling
a clock set backwards cannot hold uploads past the auth cooldown's own length
a flush with nothing queued and nothing pending sends nothing
page hide sends the pending batch under its own batch_id, and keeps it until an acknowledgement
page hide with nothing pending seals and persists a batch before sending it, and a second hide sends that same batch
page hide sends nothing while either gate is closed
